subject: MAP: acceptance cadence, artifact provenance gates and delivery
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@retailnova.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RetailNova MAP and evaluation artifacts handoff

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency and the per-route cost visibility. Per our conversation, attaching a first-pass MAP (summary) and a small sample of the evaluation assets we want to share for the pilot: a 500-record promptpack and a minimal testcase manifest.

High-level asks from RetailNova:
- Access window: 90 days from handoff for engineering review + one production-rehearsal run.
- Usage constraints: no redistribution outside the pilot team; no public release of promptpack.
- Provenance: we need a simple manifest linking samples to business categories and explicit deletion instructions after the acceptance window.

Next steps we proposed on call:
1) Redwood to confirm acceptance criteria and any additional security controls (audit logs, ephemeral credentials).
2) Agree on delivery mechanism + staging bucket + retention.
3) Sign MAP/Statement of Work (DocuSign).

I've attached: retailnova_map_v1.pdf (draft MAP), promptpack_sample.zip (100-record sample), testcase_manifest.csv (schema and labels). Legal (cc'd) may send redlines to the MAP.

Claire
RetailNova — Head of AI Partnerships

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@retailnova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RetailNova MAP and evaluation artifacts handoff

Claire — thanks for the packet and clear asks. Quick notes from our side and proposed acceptance cadence: 

Thanks for the sample; we reviewed the manifest and the labels look straightforward. Proposed acceptance criteria for the pilot (short list):
- Completeness: all samples referenced in the manifest available in the agreed bucket and checksum-verified.
- Reproducibility: Redwood can run the provided 3 smoke testcases in our staging lane without manual edits.
- No-data-exfil: promptpack does not include PII per the manifest; if any PII is found we will flag and isolate.
- Audit logs: request-level logs for the pilot window retained for 180 days (encrypted at rest).

Timeline (proposed MAP sprint):
- 2027-04-05: final MAP sign-off (DocuSign)
- 2027-04-07: artifact handoff (staging bucket + temporary credentials)
- 2027-04-08 to 2027-05-08: engineering run and acceptance tests
- 2027-05-10: acceptance sync and go/no-go decision

Couple of clarifying Qs:
1) For the retention ask — we can retain request logs for 180 days but will need explicit confirmation that RetailNova is okay with 180 days (we can shorten to 90 if required).
2) Delivery mechanism: we favor an ephemeral GCS signed-url + per-file checksums; if RetailNova needs SFTP we can accomodate but prefer signed URLs for speed.

Marissa and Karthik are on copy for the operational details; Marissa will own the onramp checklist.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Claire — adding the operational checklist and a concrete delivery plan. Attaching the onramp checklist and the artifact manifest with checksum column filled (retailnova_map_v1.pdf, testcase_manifest.csv).

Operational checklist (owner in parens):
- Create staging GCS bucket and grant ephemeral read-only signed-URL access (Marissa)
- Upload artifacts, compute SHA256 checksums, populate manifest (RetailNova/Claire to confirm)
- Provide one service account with limited access for a 30-day token rotation (Karthik)
- Run three smoke testcases on Redwood staging lane and record results (Grace/Marissa)
- Log retention: enable request-level tracing, confirm retention window (Grace)

Usage and legal guardrails to include in MAP:
- No redistribution beyond RetailNova pilot team and Redwood engagement engineers.
- Artifacts are for evaluation only; copies must be deleted from Redwood staging after the 90-day window unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Any derivative promptpack shipments to production require a separate license.

Please confirm:
- Preferred delivery: signed URLs to bucket 'rn-eval-staging-2027' by 2027-04-07.
- Do you want us to run the smoke tests before or after you complete a blocklist review? Our recommendation: blocklist review first, then smoke tests.

Attachments: onramp_checklist.pdf (checklist), testcase_manifest.csv (with checksums), promptpack_sample.zip (sample subset).

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Manager — Redwood Inference

Cc: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@retailnova.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RetailNova MAP and evaluation artifacts handoff — security details

Looping in a couple of security clarifications for the MAP and delivery:

1) Ephemeral creds: we will issue time-limited signed URLs (7-day lifetime) and rotate the GCS key material at 30 days. For the engineering run (30 days) we can provide a short-lived service account token that is rotated automatically.

2) Audit & access logs: Redwood can provide request-level audit logs that include request id, timestamp, model, and which prompt was invoked. To meet your compliance we will:
   - Retain logs for 180 days (encrypted).
   - Provide a daily digest with counts by test-case (CSV).

3) Data access controls: to avoid accidental exfil, we'll run the pilot inside a staging lane with egress locked down and only allow outbound telemetry to our observability endpoint. If RetailNova requires additional in-line content scanning (blocklist enforcement) before running, we can pipeline that as part of the acceptance cadence.

Question for RetailNova legal (cc): do you need a separate MSA addendum for the sample promptpack / testcases, or can we cover the constraints in the MAP? If you prefer an addendum we can draft one quickly.

-Karthik
Head of Product Ops — Redwood Inference
